key_insight: VisGym provides a diverse, customizable, scalable suite of 17 environments that enable systematic evaluation and training of Vision‑Language Models on long‑horizon, multi‑step visual interaction tasks.
problem_solved: Current VLM benchmarks and toolkits poorly characterize multi‑step interaction capabilities (integration of perception, memory, and action) and lack flexible, scalable environments for training and stress‑testing long‑horizon behavior.
method: Curates 17 environments spanning symbolic puzzles, real‑image understanding, navigation, and manipulation to cover varied multimodal challenges.
Exposes flexible controls over difficulty, input representation, planning horizon, and feedback to create tailored tasks and curricula.
Provides multi‑step solvers and interfaces for training and systematic evaluation of VLMs on sequential, interactive tasks.
impact: VisGym lets practitioners probe and improve VLMs' sequential decision‑making, memory, and generalization across modalities, accelerating development of robust, interactive multimodal agents and more informative benchmark comparisons.
visual_elements: Suite overview diagram with four domain icons (puzzles, real images, navigation, manipulation) and sample tasks
Control panel infographic showing adjustable axes: difficulty, input type, planning horizon, feedback
Performance heatmap or bar chart comparing model success across tasks and horizons
Episode storyboard: a multi‑step interaction trace (observations → actions → memory) illustrating solver behavior
paper_title: VisGym: Diverse, Customizable, Scalable Environments for Multimodal Agents
paper_authors: Zirui Wang, Junyi Zhang, Jiaxin Ge, Long Lian, Letian Fu
